headline_marked: [[Orange Tsai forges Microsoft Edge full chain]] with logic bugs only, wins $175,000 at Pwn2Own
headline: Orange Tsai forges Microsoft Edge full chain with logic bugs only, wins $175,000 at Pwn2Own
summary: Security researcher Orange Tsai chained 4 logic bugs to achieve a sandbox escape on Microsoft Edge, earning $175,000 and the Pwnie Award for Epic Achievement.
details: Security researcher Orange Tsai of DEVCORE Research Team successfully chained four logic bugs to achieve a full sandbox escape on Microsoft Edge. This exploit earned him $175,000 and 17.5 Master of Pwn points at Pwn2Own Berlin 2026.

The complete exploit chain comprised five bugs and two Windows features, notably achieved without any memory corruption or AI assistance. This feat was recognized with a Pwnie Award for Epic Achievement, highlighting its unique, human-crafted nature.

The journey began by examining Chromium's 'navigation' process and a lesser-known component called 'Navigation Throttles.' These throttles, residing in the Browser Process, intercept all navigation requests, a corner of the browser often overlooked by researchers.

Tsai discovered a specific throttle in Microsoft Edge called `EdgeCAGuidanceNavigationThrottle`, designed for its enterprise Entra ID feature. This throttle aims to guide users to the correct User Profile when signing in with a work account on Microsoft websites, activating from specific Microsoft-owned origins like `login.live.com`.

The throttle's vulnerability lies in its handling of attacker-controlled query strings: if conditions are met, it cancels the original navigation and launches a new one using a URL from the query string. This new navigation is initiated by the Browser Process, not the Renderer.

This browser-initiated navigation allowed access to normally prohibited pages such as `edge://settings` or `devtools://...`, and even pseudo-schemes like `javascript:alert(origin)`. Initially, the `javascript:` primitive's full potential was underestimated.

The turning point came with the realization that the new navigation, being initiated by the Browser Process, offered significantly more control than a Renderer-initiated one. This crucial insight enabled the development of a full chain exploit, demonstrating the power of logic-only vulnerabilities.

headline_marked: [[Claude Code sends agent transcripts]] to its model every 30s, consuming up to 26% of spend
headline: Claude Code sends agent transcripts to its model every 30s, consuming up to 26% of spend
summary: Claude Code's background agents automatically send their full transcripts to their models every 30 seconds, a hidden process that can consume 18-26% of your rate-limit headroom. This feature has been on by default since August 2026.
details: Claude Code's background agents automatically transmit their entire transcript to their assigned model (usually Opus) every 30 seconds. This hidden process, detected via OpenTelemetry exports, can consume a significant portion of a user's rate-limit headroom, estimated at 18-26%.

The purpose of these frequent transmissions is to update the agent's status line in the UI with a 3-5 word summary of its most recent action. Crucially, this information never reaches the main conversation or the user's model directly.

This automatic summary feature has been enabled by default since version 2.1.232 (August 2026) and lacks any user-facing setting to disable it. Multiple independent measurements have confirmed the substantial resource consumption.

A community-developed Bun preload script, `no-agent-summary.js`, offers a workaround. This ~80-line script intercepts `setTimeout`/`setInterval` calls, identifying and disabling the specific timers responsible for the agent summary transmissions.

The script works by recognizing a unique string within the callback's source text, a method necessary because the Claude Code module is shipped as precompiled Bun bytecode, preventing simpler modifications or API client interception.

To implement the fix, users need to place the script in a stable location and set the `BUN_OPTIONS` environment variable globally to preload it. This requires restarting the Claude Code daemon and any active sessions.

Verification involves checking for "preload active mode=off" on startup and confirming that `query_source = agent_summary` requests remain at zero in OpenTelemetry exports. This ensures the timer suppression is active.

Flamerix AI provides this MIT-licensed tool "as is," warning that future Claude Code updates could silently re-enable the summary feature if the internal callback string changes. Users are responsible for checking service terms.
This project is independent and is not affiliated with, sponsored or endorsed by Anthropic, PBC.
